title: fix(spec,objectql)!: retire `scale` from the currency field type — refused at parse, no longer enforced on writes
body:
Fixes #19629

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Executes maintainer ruling `5791803339` (batch #215 item 1, letter B, 「215 同意」): `scale` is retired from the `currency` field type. The consumer half (field designer, grid summary footer) is objectstack-ai/objectui#10221 and is not in this diff. B′ (enforcing `currencyConfig.precision` on writes) was not taken and is not here.

## What changes

1. **`@objectstack/spec`, `FieldSchema`** (`packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`): `scale` on a `type: 'currency'` field is refused at parse. The check follows the file's per-type `superRefine` house pattern: one `custom` issue at `scale`, whose remedy names `currencyConfig.precision`. No alias, no grace window. The remedy says to delete the key by default. It says to move the value to `currencyConfig.precision` only when the field already declares a `currencyConfig`, and warns against adding a `currencyConfig` just to carry the value (see reading 1 below). The `scale` describe now names the set the key still applies to: `number`, `percent`, `rating` and `slider`, enforced on writes, and `formula`, rounded.
2. **`@objectstack/objectql`, record validator** (`packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts`): the `max_scale` branch no longer reads `def.scale` for `currency`, so the type leaves the enforced set. `min`, `max` and the finite-number check still apply to currency. `percent`, `number`, `rating` and `slider` are unchanged.
3. **ADR-0087 semantic entry** `field-currency-scale-refused` (`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.field-currency-scale-refused.ts`). It covers stored metadata: delete the key, or move the value to `currencyConfig.precision` on a field that already declares that block. `registry.ts` was regenerated with `gen:migration-registry`, and `check:migration-registry` is green.
4. **Shipped examples** that the refusal would reject. `scale: 2` was deleted from each; none needed a move, because the only two sites with a `currencyConfig` already carried `precision: 2`:
   - `examples/app-crm/src/objects/account.object.ts`, `opportunity.object.ts`, `opportunity-line-item.object.ts` (×2)
   - `examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/account.object.ts`, `client-brief.object.ts`, `expense-report.object.ts`, `external/customer.object.ts`, `external/order.object.ts`, `field-zoo.object.ts`, `invoice.object.ts` (×3), `project.object.ts` (×2)
5. **Documentation examples.** `scale: 2` was deleted from 13 currency examples in `content/docs/concepts/architecture.mdx` (×2), `concepts/metadata-driven.mdx` (×2), `data-modeling/fields.mdx`, `data-modeling/objects.mdx`, `data-modeling/schema-design.mdx`, `protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`, `protocol/objectql/schema.mdx` (×4) and `protocol/objectql/types.mdx`. The `schema.mdx` property table's `scale` row no longer lists `currency`.
6. **Generated**, via `check:generated --fix`, never hand-edited: `content/docs/references/data/field.mdx`, `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`, `content/docs/references/system/migration.mdx` (the `scale` describe). `authorable-surface`, `api-surface`, `json-schema.manifest`, `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide did not move: no key or export was added or removed.
7. **`packages/spec/src/data/field-scale.ts`**: the docblock's `currency` bullet claimed `CurrencyConfigSchema.precision` is the money faces' authored override. That is false at the pin (reading 1 below), and the bullet now records the retirement instead.

## Measured first, on `origin/main` `1f89ba0d70` (built `dist`)

- A currency field with `scale: 2` **parses today**: `FieldSchema.safeParse` succeeds. Control: the same with `type: 'number'` also succeeds.
- The record validator **refuses** a currency write over `scale` today: `scale: 2`, write `1.234` → `max_scale {"scale":2,"actual":3}`, "F must have at most 2 decimal places (got 3)". A currency field without `scale` accepts `1.23456`.
- `max_scale` reads `def.scale` on **all four** controls. Each was given `scale: 2` and the write `1.23456`: `number`, `rating` and `slider` answer `{scale:2, actual:5}`, and `percent` answers `{scale:4, actual:5}` because of the fraction-storage derivation.
- **Population census**: a TypeScript AST sweep over every tracked `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.mjs`/`.js` file (7,036 files; 323 mention `currency`, 171 currency object literals, 24 `Field.currency` calls). It found **15 example sites**, all listed above, and **7 test fixtures**, listed below. A JSON walk over 556 tracked `.json` files found 0 currency-typed objects with `scale`. A windowed scan of 831 `.md`/`.mdx` files found the 13 documentation examples. There are 0 hits in `skills/`, `packages/platform-objects`, seeds or any committed JSON fixture. The one surviving AST hit, `packages/spec/src/data/inline-related-columns.test.ts:103`, is `InlineGridColumnSchema.scale`: an inline grid column's own rounding key, a different schema that the ruling does not cover.

## ⚠️ Readings that differ from the ruling's, reported and not acted on

1. **`currencyConfig.precision` has no reader.** No face in the pinned console (`.objectui-sha` `62597c588072`) reads it, and no non-test code in this repo does. At that pin, the currency cell (`CurrencyCellRenderer` → `formatCurrency(value, currency, locale)`) uses only the currency's ISO 4217 minor unit. The edit widget (`packages/fields/src/widgets/CurrencyField.tsx:76-77`) reads the **field-level** `precision`, and its own comment says `currencyConfig.precision` is "a different key on the `currencyConfig` block that this widget never reads". This repo's liveness ledger records the same (`precision` live through that widget; `currencyConfig` live through `defaultCurrency` only). The ruling's reading "cell → the currency's ISO minor units / `currencyConfig.precision`" therefore does not hold at the pin. Adding a bare `currencyConfig` to carry a moved value also materializes `defaultCurrency: 'CNY'`, which changes the resolved display currency. I executed the remedy as ruled, naming `currencyConfig.precision`, but wrote it so that following it cannot trigger that currency flip. Whether the remedy should name that key, the field-level `precision`, or no key is an open question for the seat.
2. **The ruling's control reading, "`examples/**` holds 2 currency fields, 0 declare `scale`", undercounts.** Fifteen `Field.currency` declarations in `examples/` declared `scale: 2`. The ruling's count appears to cover only `type: 'currency'` literals. All fifteen had `max_scale` write enforcement until this change.
3. **A fourth face.** The pinned console's dashboard `ObjectMetricWidget` currency arm reads `valueFieldDef.scale ?? 0` (`packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectMetricWidget.tsx:229`). That face is not in the ruling's list and not in objectui#10221's ruled scope. On the 15 example fields, the grid summary footer and the metric widget render currency with **zero decimals** between this landing and the objectui#10221 pin bump.
4. **Direction of the validator half.** It moves writes from refused to accepted. The #19320 precedent declared a `max_scale` allowance change of that direction `yes (widening)`. The ruling says `no` (a narrowing), so this PR declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` as ruled.

## Tests, on HEAD `7c0a33c6ad`

Every command went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`. Each count is the runner's own summary line.

- `@objectstack/spec` `vitest run --project local`: **527 files, 15509 passed, 1 todo**. `--project repo`: **35 files, 602 passed**. Both ran at `a5858edbb6`. The one later commit, `7c0a33c6ad`, changes only a docblock line in `field-scale.ts`.
- `@objectstack/objectql` `vitest run --project local`: **305 files, 5093 passed**. `--project repo`: **1 file, 5 passed**.
- `@objectstack/platform-objects`: 54 files, 883 passed. `@objectstack/metadata-core`: 16 files, 285 passed. `@objectstack/driver-sql`: 179 files passed, 11 skipped; 2645 tests passed, 168 skipped. `@objectstack/service-automation`: 142 files, 1697 passed, including the `.integration.test.ts` oracle, which is in the default include. `@objectstack/example-crm`: 5 files, 45 passed. `@objectstack/example-showcase`: 29 files, 384 passed.
- `typecheck` passed (exit 0) for `spec` (with its `check:test-typecheck`: 53 files / 255 errors / 142 pinned signatures held), `objectql`, `metadata-core`, `driver-sql`, `service-automation`, `example-crm` and `example-showcase`.
- Build: `turbo run build` over `./packages/*`, `./packages/*/*` and `./examples/*`: **73 successful, 73 total**. The showcase and CRM example builds parse every object, so they compile clean under the refusal.
- Before the change, on BASE `1f89ba0d70` `dist`, a node probe gave the readings listed under "Measured first".

## Reverse verification

Both runs are one-shot proofs from the committed state. The file was restored to its `BASE` blob (`1f89ba0d70`), the landing was proved by blob hash, the pin was run, and the file was restored with `git checkout HEAD --`. The restore was proved by hash equality with the HEAD blob and an empty `git diff HEAD`, with a trap on EXIT/INT/TERM. Both test files resolve their subject through a relative `src` import, so no rebuild was involved.

- `field.zod.ts` at BASE (blob `cc96254284`) → `field-currency-scale-refused.test.ts`: **5 failed | 3 passed**. The four refusal pins and the describe pin went red, and the three controls stayed green. Restored: blob `0c24baa382` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
- `record-validator.ts` at BASE (blob `2e2d3981d2`) → `record-validator.test.ts`: **1 failed | 111 passed**. Only the change pin ("accepts the same write when a legacy currency def still carries `scale`") went red. The unchanged-contract pin (no width declared → accepted), the `min`/`max`/finite pin and the `number`/`percent` controls stayed green, as designed. Restored: blob `c200751358` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Test fixtures re-judged

These fixtures pinned a currency field with `scale`, or `max_scale` on currency:

- `packages/spec/src/data/field.test.ts`: "should accept **number** field with precision and scale" spelled `type: 'currency'`. It now spells `number`, a spelling change only.
- `packages/spec/src/data/object.test.ts`: the account fixture's `annual_revenue` lost `scale: 2`.
- `packages/spec/src/data/field-scale.test.ts`: the resolver's "declared scale wins" example moved from `currency` to `slider`, and a comment repeating the false override claim was corrected.
- `packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.test.ts`: the #19320 CONTROLS loop dropped `currency`, and a new #19629 block holds the three ruled pins.
- `packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-field-expression-scale.integration.test.ts`: the #11060 oracle needs a live `scale` gate, so its `total` field moved from `currency` to `number`. The subject is unchanged.
- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-external-unprovisioned-sort-anchor.test.ts` (it parses through `ObjectSchema.create`) and `packages/metadata-core/test/injected-column-provenance.test.ts`: both mirror the showcase external customer, and both lost `scale: 2`.

## Changeset

`.changeset/19629-currency-scale-retired.md` sets `@objectstack/spec: minor` and `@objectstack/objectql: minor`, with a **BREAKING** banner. Per AGENTS.md, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is a breaking change, and the launch-window convention ships an accept-set narrowing as `minor`, never `major`: `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major`. The precedents are #18972, which declared `no (narrowing)` minor for the `scale` ceiling, and #19320, which made an objectql `max_scale` allowance change minor. The changeset carries the FROM → TO table and the ADR-0087 disposition marker `registered field-currency-scale-refused`. `check-adr-0087-registration` reads it as `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing]`. The test-only packages (`driver-sql`, `metadata-core`, `service-automation`) ship nothing that changed. The examples are private.

## Acceptance notes

- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/records-forms.json`: the field-zoo fixture line still reads "f_currency scale 2". Its `knownGaps` text, which says `scale` is not enforced on write, has been stale since #7501. This is checklist-owned text and was left for that seat.
- Four documentation YAML examples keep `precision: 18` on a currency field (`schema.mdx` ×3, `types.mdx`). They are meant as DECIMAL(18,2) total digits, but the pinned edit widget reads field-level `precision` on currency as fraction digits. This predates this change and was not touched, so the examples still carry that mismatch.
- `FieldSchema`'s alias table renames `decimals` / `decimalPlaces` to `scale`. On a currency field that rename now leads to this refusal, whose remedy carries the author on.
- hotcrm declares `scale: 2` on a currency quote field (hotcrm#1206, cited by the flow oracle). That becomes a refused parse downstream; the migration entry covers it.

## Gates, on HEAD `7c0a33c6ad`

- The derived families come from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`: **119**. Every one was run on `7c0a33c6ad` with its exit code captured before any pipe, and **all 119 exited 0**. `--ran` reconciliation: "119 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 119 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 119 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)".
- Three families answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3) on a partial build: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt` and `check:skill-examples`. They are counted above only from their re-run after the full build, where each exited 0.
- `check:objectui-pin-citations` found one real problem in the new docblock, a pin cited in an unrecognised spelling. It was corrected in `7c0a33c6ad` and is green.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: "All 15 generated artifacts are up to date".
- `check-adr-0087-registration`: `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] registered field-currency-scale-refused`. `check-changeset-no-major`: no `major` bump. The level axis reads this PR body, so it was NOT MEASURED locally.
- Lint was narrowed to the diff and was not repo-wide. `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 24 changed `.ts`/`.mjs` files reported 24 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings and no ignore notices. The narrowing holds because `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting (its own comment at lines 326-328: no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The full `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.
